staff.bio: Dr. Nyeisha DeWitt is an investor, serial entrepreneur and CEO of Oakland Natives Give Back Fund, Inc., which she founded in 2008 to exemplify an evolved concept of philanthropy and raise awareness around the importance of daily attendance. Her unique background and personal journey uncovered the greatest crack in the foundation of a child’s success: chronic absenteeism, and has given her the ability to see it from a multitude of perspectives.  She is a high school dropout, an educator, a mother of children with unique learning abilities, and a funder who supports using out-of-the-box thinking to research solutions and combat this national crisis. Since inception, ONGB has invested nearly $7M in resources toward that end.</br>Nyeisha holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Sociology from the University of California, Berkeley. Dr. Kimberly Mayfield is a revered educator, scholar and published author with over 30 years of experience in K-12 schools and higher education. She holds two teaching credentials and a Master of Arts in teaching. Dr. Mayfield received her doctorate in Learning and Instruction from the University of San Francisco. Her research interests and activism are focused on creating a permanent diverse teaching force, reducing chronic absenteeism in public schools and reducing the over identification of African American students who receive special education services. From 2006-2012 Dr. Mayfield was a co-convener of the Effective Teachers for Oakland community taskforce. She has trained hundreds of teachers who are currently working in San Francisco Bay Area schools districts. Dr. Mayfield has also provided professional development workshops to teachers, administrators and district personnel in the areas of her research agenda.  She was the first African American to earn tenure at Holy Names University (HNU). Over her 21 year career at HNU she served in the following roles: assistant professor, associate professor, chair of the Education Department, dean of the School of Education and Liberal Arts, and Vice President for Strategic Partnerships and External Relations. Dr. Mayfield has been recognized by the Oakland/Bay Area chapter of the National Coalition of 100 Black Women and  Congresswoman Barbara Lee, for working to improve educational outcomes for students in Oakland CA . She is past board chair of the  Oakland Alliance of Community Partnerships; Oakland Natives give Back Fund, Inc., former president of the Oakland/Berkeley chapter of Black Women Organized for Political Action (BWOPA) and former Deputy Mayor for the city of Oakland CA.  Presently, Dr. Mayfield serves on the state board of BWOPA as an education policy adviser and professional development consultant for the West Contra Costa Unified School District.</br>Dr. Kimberly Mayfield is a respected educator, scholar, and author with over 30 years of experience in K-12 and higher education. She holds two teaching credentials, a master’s in teaching, and a doctorate in Learning and Instruction from the University of San Francisco. Her work focuses on creating a diverse teaching force, reducing chronic absenteeism, and addressing the over-identification of African American students in special education. Dr. Mayfield was the first African American to earn tenure at Holy Names University, where she served in multiple leadership roles. She continues to advise on education policy and provide professional development for school districts across the Bay Area.

Yuri Hernández Osorio (she/her) is the new Vice President for Program at Oakland Natives Give Back (ONGB). Originally from Toluca, México, Yuri’s family is from Puebla, and she identifies more closely with that region. She has a passion for travel and live music. Yuri holds a degree in social work from the University of Michigan, with areas of specialization that include immigration, equity, diversity, professional development, and the management of human services. She has spent the majority of her career in higher education, most recently serving at the University of California, Berkeley. Yuri currently lives in Oakland and deeply appreciates all that the Bay Area has to offer.
